title: What If You Lived on Mars for a Whole Year?

scenes.text: What if you spent a year on Mars? The day would feel familiar. Almost nothing else would.
A Martian day is 24 hours and 39 minutes, but a Martian year lasts 687 Earth days.
Gravity is only 38 percent of Earth's, so a 100 pound person would weigh about 38 pounds.
The air is 95 percent carbon dioxide, under one percent as thick as ours, and averages minus 64 degrees Fahrenheit.
Radiation on the surface is about 0.64 millisieverts a day, roughly 230 over a year, with nothing overhead to stop it.
Add the trips there and back, and a full mission adds up to about one sievert, the entire career limit set by the European Space Agency.
